trust_decision.summary: With permitSetMultiParamEntries, caller-supplied object keys are trusted as column identifiers and wrapped in backticks without doubling embedded backticks, in three separate client-side SQL text builders.

landing_point.why: The summary names SET expansion via permitSetMultiParamEntries; conn.query('UPDATE t SET ?', obj) is the documented use and Query.start inlines the top-level object expansion.

fix_sites.entry_point: connection.query / pool.query (promise and callback APIs) with a top-level object parameter, text protocol
connection.query with an object nested inside an array or object parameter (lib/cmd/query.js:134, lib/cmd/query.js:234), or any parameter following a stream parameter (lib/cmd/query.js:345)
fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation: shared text encoder (recursive writeParam)

fix_sites.entry_point: connection.escape(value) / pool.escape(value) public string-formatting API (lib/connection.js:111, lib/pool.js:719)
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level public API / string formatter in misc utils

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/misc/utils.js:219 (connection.escape / pool.escape, a client-side formatter that never sends SQL itself; also second_implementation at lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:150 reached only via nested or post-stream params)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: escape() only returns a string and never executes a query, so a solver can argue the caller owns what it does with it; text-encoder.js:150 looks unreachable for SET ? because Query.start handles top-level objects inline.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Keys must stay always-backtick-quoted so reserved words (e.g. `order`) and non-ASCII names still expand; objects must still fall back to a quoted JSON string when the option is off or the object is empty; toSqlString/null/Buffer values inside the object must keep their encoding. Stripping or rejecting keys (as sessionVariables does) or throwing like Utils.escapeId on empty/NUL keys would break legitimate column names.

O6_input_shapes: object nested in an array parameter or as a value inside another object (text-encoder recursion)
object parameter after a stream parameter (_paramWritten -> TextEncoder.writeParam)
object passed to connection.escape / pool.escape (utils.js); fix also replaces this.escape(val) with recursive escapeParameters for nested values

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an inline copy of the object-key expansion in _paramWritten (post-stream params) instead of delegating to TextEncoder.writeParam
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Query.start already inlines the same switch for speed (lib/cmd/query.js:86-241); a maintainer optimising the stream path the same way would copy the raw '`' + key + '`' concatenation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: sessionVariables keys emitted as backtick/@@-quoted identifiers without doubling, instead of the current character strip
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same identifier-from-object-key concept in connection setup; a maintainer allowing exotic variable names would swap the strip for naive quoting.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: permitSetMultiParamEntries-style key expansion added to the binary/execute or batch text-rewrite path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Feature parity request for execute()/batch(); the binary encoder currently JSON-stringifies objects, so a parity patch would reintroduce key interpolation in another file.

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-89) via unescaped identifier built from object keys
